answer:
VERDICT. Your two options are not the real alternatives. In the CRM the removal and the new identity are one and the same record: a single sampling activity, instantiated under more than one class, that both diminished the moth and brought the extract into existence. Record the extract as its own object with its own identifier. The tie back to the paratype is carried by that activity, not by shared identity, so it survives the choice — indeed it only becomes traceable once the extract has an identity of its own. What the choice does settle is that the extract is not itself the paratype; it is material derived from the paratype.

WHY "UNDER THE SPECIMEN'S EXISTING IDENTITY" CANNOT WORK. Every property the CRM offers here presupposes two distinct instances: P112 diminished points at the thing made smaller, P113 removed at the thing taken off; in CRMsci, O1 diminished at the source and O5 removed at the sample. If both ends are the same instance there is nothing to say. E80 Part Removal's scope note settles the case directly: where the removed part had no discernible identity before removal but does have one afterwards, the same activity is to be recorded as both an E80 Part Removal and an E12 Production. CRMsci's S1 Matter Removal (the class the CRM puts above both E80 Part Removal and S2 Sample Taking) says the same in sampling vocabulary: removed matter may acquire a persistent identity of a different nature beyond the act of removal, and such cases are to be modelled by multiple instantiation with the adequate creation concept. Note also that P46 is composed of is simply false after the clipping (the extract is not currently part of the moth), and the CRM has no "was formerly part of" shortcut — Martin Doerr raised exactly that gap for missing parts (t1749) and it was left unresolved. The event is the record of former part-hood.

THE MOTH — identity unchanged. E20 Biological Object, keeping its drawer number (P1 is identified by / P48 has preferred identifier → E42 Identifier). Its paratype status stays exactly where it has always been, on the specimen: P137 exemplifies → the taxon (E55 Type), with P137.1 in the taxonomic role = 'paratype'. P137 exists for precisely this purpose — "P137 was introduced to deal with type specimens in natural history" (t0375, message 5); the CRM's own P137 example is a Clayton Herbarium sheet exemplifying a species in the taxonomic role lectotype. If you want the 1932 act on the record, the species description is an E83 Type Creation, P135 created type → the taxon and P136 was based on → this specimen (P136 also carries a .1 taxonomic role; the published example uses 'original element'). E83's scope note is explicit that in the life sciences type creation requires an exemplary specimen and a published type definition. Sampling does not make the moth human-made: closing this very point on E80/P112, Martin Doerr reported the SIG had decided the alternative violates class identity criteria — "It just leaves a human-made feature on a natural object" (t1536). So the moth stays an E20; if you want the damage itself on the record, that is a human-made feature (E25) on the specimen, or simply P44 has condition / a condition assessment.

THE ACTIVITY — one instance, three classes. S2 Sample Taking (CRMsci): matter taken from a material substantial for further analysis. E80 Part Removal: the specimen was physically diminished and modified. E12 Production: the extract came into existence. Properties: O3 sampled from → the moth (CRMsci declares E18 Physical Thing a subclass of S10 Material Substantial, so a pinned insect is a legitimate range value); O4 sampled at → E53 Place, the spot on the specimen, i.e. which leg; O1 diminished and its subproperty P112 diminished → the moth; O2/O5 removed and P113 removed → the matter taken off / the sample; P31 has modified → the moth; P108 has produced and P92 brought into existence → the extract; P14 carried out by → the graduate student; P4 has time-span → last year; P32 used general technique / P33 used specific technique → the barcoding protocol. That the CRM intends this for natural-history sampling is visible in its own examples: P112 diminished's example is "The coral of the Cocos Islands (E20) was diminished by the removal of the Porite coral specimen by Charles Darwin (E80)", and P112's range was deliberately widened from E24 Physical Human-Made Thing to E18 Physical Thing under Issue 574 (status Done, changes in v7.1.2/v7.2.1) so that natural specimens can be the thing diminished.

THE EXTRACT — new object, new number. E24 Physical Human-Made Thing and S13 Sample. E24 because its scope note assigns to E24 the results of preparation of natural history specimens that substantially change their natural or original state — dissolving a leg into a DNA extract is such a preparation — and because P108 has produced, which the CRM quantifies as necessary on E12, ranges over E24. S13 Sample because its whole intension is matter taken from a source to be representative of that source's material qualities: that is what makes the tube a document of the moth rather than just some liquid, and S11 Amount of Matter (its parent) is designed for content that acquires identity by confinement rather than by stability of form, which is what a tube in a -80C freezer provides. Its own catalogue number: P1 is identified by / P48 has preferred identifier → E42 Identifier (record the cataloguing itself as E15 Identifier Assignment if you want the act attributed). Being biological material it may also be co-instantiated as E20 Biological Object — the same dual reading the CRM already allows for prepared specimens such as butterfly frames. Location: P53 has former or current location (or CRMsci's O15 occupied) → the freezer as E53 Place; avoid P55/P54, whose domain is E19.

OPTIONAL, IF YOU WANT THE CLIPPED LEG ON THE RECORD. E24's scope note permits describing the production also as an E81 Transformation to document that matter and structure continue from the original into the product (P124 transformed → the leg; P123 resulted in → the extract). That requires treating the leg as a documented thing that ceased to exist, an identity nobody in your case assigned. Since only the extract was catalogued, I would not do it, and would let the single sampling activity carry the story. Do not reach for E81 for the moth: E81 destroys its input, and the moth survives.

THE PARATYPE QUESTION, DIRECTLY. No — giving the extract its own identity costs you nothing, and reusing the specimen's identity would buy you nothing. 'Paratype' is a nomenclatural role held by the specimen designated in 1932; nothing in the CRM propagates P137 exemplifies down a part-removal chain, and I found no property that would. The claim "this extract came from the paratype" is a path, and it is intact: extract ← O5 removed / P113 removed ← the 2025 sampling activity → O3 sampled from / P112 diminished → the moth → P137 exemplifies (taxonomic role paratype) → the taxon; and, independently, the 1932 E83 Type Creation P136 was based on the moth, which a later clipping cannot alter. What you must not do is copy P137 onto the extract: that would assert the extract is a paratype, which is false and, being a monotonic assertion in the knowledge base, unfixable later. If your system needs 'material of the paratype of X' as a stated curatorial claim rather than an inferred path, record it as an E13 Attribute Assignment (or E17 Type Assignment) so the assertion is attributed to you. Two practical corollaries: aliquots of the extract are a further sampling of the extract, not of the moth — CRMsci provides S24 Sample Splitting with O27 split and O29 removed sub-sample for exactly that; and sample identity is tied to the qualities the sample is meant to witness, which is why samples "can be split without loosing their identity" (Martin Doerr, t1080) but stop being that sample when those qualities are corrupted (S13's scope note).

rejected_alternatives.option: Recording the extract under the pinned moth's existing identity (same instance, same identifier)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P112 diminished / P113 removed and CRMsci's O1 diminished / O5 removed each need two distinct instances; with one instance there is no statement left to make. It would also assert that a tube in a -80C freezer and a moth in a drawer are one physical thing, contradicting their separate identifiers, locations and custody, and P46 is composed of no longer holds once the leg is off. The CRM has no 'was formerly part of' shortcut to fall back on (t1749, unresolved).

rejected_alternatives.option: E81 Transformation for the sampling event
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E81 requires simultaneous destruction and creation, with the input losing its identity. The moth survives the clipping with its identity and catalogue number intact, so it is not transformed. E81 is defensible only for the narrower step of the leg being dissolved into the extract, and only if you first give the clipped leg an identity of its own — which nobody did here. E24's scope note allows adding E81 to a production to document material continuity, i.e. as an addition to E12, never as a replacement for it.

rejected_alternatives.option: E6 Destruction of the leg plus an unrelated E12 Production of the extract
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Two disconnected events lose the very thing you are asking about: the derivation link. E6 takes a thing out of existence but records nothing about what was made from it, so nothing would connect the extract to the paratype. The CRM's design intent is the opposite — E80's scope note describes the class as a basis for reasoning about continuity of identity of objects removed from other objects.

rejected_alternatives.option: Copying P137 exemplifies (taxonomic role paratype) onto the extract
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P137 declares one particularly characteristic example of a type; the paratype is the insect examined in 1932, not a 2025 laboratory preparation. No property found in the tools propagates P137 to parts or products, and asserting it would be a false statement the knowledge base cannot retract monotonically. Derivation is expressed by the sampling event, which is what 'comes from the paratype' actually means.

rejected_alternatives.option: S3 Measurement by Sampling for the barcoding workflow
rejected_alternatives.why_not: S3 is for taking a sample and analysing it as one unit of activity where the sample is typically not identified or preserved beyond that activity. Here the extract has its own catalogue number and sits in a freezer, so it must be identified and preserved — exactly the case S3 says it need not instantiate O5 removed for.

rejected_alternatives.option: E11 Modification alone for the clipping
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E11 records that the specimen was altered but names nothing that was taken off and nothing that came into existence, so the extract would have no documented origin. Its subclasses E80 and E12 exist to add precisely those two statements.

siblings_considered.why_not: E22 Human-Made Object is the other subclass of E19 Physical Object and is the rival a curator would raise, since the specimen is a pinned, mounted preparation. But the thing that was sampled and that carries the paratype role is the insect, a natural product of a living organism, and the SIG explicitly decided that sampling a natural object does not make it human-made — it leaves a human-made feature on it (t1536). E22 may be co-instantiated for the mount as a whole (the CRM's own butterfly-frame case under E20), but it cannot replace E20 here.

A1 Excavation Processing Unit is the other CRMarchaeo/CRMbase-external subclass of S1 Matter Removal alongside S2 (concept A1 shows Subclass of: S1, S4, E12, E64). It models progressive removal and recording of matter at an excavation location, coupled with observation. Nothing here is an excavation: this is a targeted laboratory subsample of a curated specimen, with a sampling spot on the object rather than a stratigraphic or trench extent.

E79 Part Addition is E80's sibling under E11 Modification and is genuinely not a plausible rival — nothing was added to the moth. I name it as required because the rival a knowledgeable reader would actually raise, E81 Transformation, is not a sibling of E80 (it sits under E63/E64 with E12) and is dealt with in rejected_alternatives and under E12 below.

E81 Transformation, E12's sibling under E63 Beginning of Existence, is the strongest rival: matter is preserved from the leg into the extract while identity is not. It is rejected as the class of this activity because E81 requires the destruction of its input, and the pinned moth — the thing the activity acts on — continues to exist under its original number. E81 only becomes relevant for a leg-as-object step nobody catalogued, and E24's scope note frames it as something added to a production, not a substitute for it.

E19 Physical Object (with its subclass E20) is E24's sibling under E18 Physical Thing and is what you would use if the extract were simply a natural object. It is not sufficient: E24's scope note assigns results of natural-history preparation that substantially change the specimen's natural state to E24, and P108 has produced — necessary on E12 Production — ranges over E24, so E19 alone cannot be the product of the production. E19/E20 can be co-instantiated to record that the content is biological; it cannot carry the 'made by a laboratory procedure' intension.

S12 Amount of Fluid is the other subclass of S11 Amount of Matter and describes the extract's physical state well — a liquid that acquires identity by being kept in a container. But S12 carries no notion of having been taken from a source to be representative of it, which is the entire documentary point of this tube and is S13 Sample's intension (and what O3 sampled from / O5 removed attach to). S12 is an optional co-instantiation, not a replacement.
Exempt: the dossier for E83 Type Creation states it is the only subclass of E65 Creation, so it has no siblings to weigh.

notes: Two tool gaps. (1) `connect S2 E20` returns no sampling properties, although CRMsci declares E18 Physical Thing a subclass of S10 Material Substantial (visible in the S10 dossier's 'Superclass of: S11, S14, E18' line), which is what licenses O3 sampled from and O1 diminished pointing at a pinned insect. The connect command appears not to walk that cross-model subclass edge downward, so the central CRMsci link for this case had to be inferred from the S10 dossier rather than read off connect. (2) `concept S24` returns 'No such concept', yet S24 Sample Splitting is the declared domain of O27 split and O29 removed sub-sample and is listed as a subclass of S2 in the S2 dossier; the sample-splitting proposal is also visible as issue 332 and thread t1427. I cite O27/O29 because they resolve, but I could not read S24's own scope note. Also worth flagging: `search.py quote` accepts thread and document-chunk ids but not concept ids, so scope-note wording from E80, S1, E12 and E24 could not be verified with quote; I have therefore paraphrased all scope-note content rather than quoting it, and reserved quotation marks for the three mailing-list phrases I did verify. One substantive residual uncertainty: E12 Production quantifies P108 has produced (range E24) as necessary, so instantiating the sampling activity as E12 commits you to treating the extract as an E24 Physical Human-Made Thing. E24's scope note supports that for natural-history preparations, but it does sit oddly beside S13 Sample / S11 Amount of Matter, whose whole point is content that need not have a stable form. If an institution finds that combination uncomfortable, the CRMsci-only route (S2 Sample Taking with O1 diminished / O5 removed and the extract as S13 Sample alone, brought into existence by P92) says everything this case needs without E12 or E24.
